c127b57119.q: How should banks customize AI agents for AML compliance when the same activity can be suspicious at one bank but normal at another?
c127b57119.a: Banks should onboard AI agents the same way they onboard humans: provide context on what the bank does, what products and customers it serves, what normal transaction patterns look like, what has historically been suspicious, and provide the necessary system logins and policy guidelines. Agents learn from this institutional knowledge just like new employees, with feedback loops that allow them to refine their decision-making over time.

0cf4db8bdb.q: What role does human-in-the-loop oversight play in AI automation for anti-money laundering compliance?
0cf4db8bdb.a: While AI agents can functionally perform AML review better than most humans in terms of quality, speed and consistency, regulators require human oversight for critical decisions. The key is having proper controls, independent validation, and human feedback loops. Banks should use AI to improve efficiency and quality of SARs submission while maintaining human approval before filing, rather than moving directly from an alert to SAR filing without any human intervention.
